chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Miskīn, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no salat after al-ʿAṣr until you perform al-Maghrib, and there is no salat after al-Fajr until the sun rises.

The proper way to understand these reports and others similar to them is one of two things: either that they are to be understood as taqiyyah, because they agree with the doctrines of the ʿāmmah; or that they are to be understood as indicating the dislikedness of beginning the nawāfil in these two times, even if that is not prohibited, because a concession has been narrated regarding the permissibility of beginning the nawāfil in these two times.

key_terms.ابْتِدَاءِ: the initiation or commencement of an act, here the nawāfil
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity in circumstances requiring it
key_terms.النَّوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers beyond the obligatory salat
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general Sunni populace or their legal schools in contrast to Shia teachings
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: a concession indicating allowance or ease in the ruling
key_terms.كَرَاهَةِ: dislikedness in legal valuation, without reaching prohibition
key_terms.لَا صَلَاةَ: a negation of prayer here referring to a legal restriction on performing salat at certain times

ai.seo_question: Are nawāfil after al-Fajr and al-ʿAṣr prohibited or merely disliked in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on performing supererogatory prayers after al-ʿAṣr and after al-Fajr. It explains that such reports are understood either as taqiyyah due to their agreement with the ʿāmmah, or as indicating karāhah rather than prohibition, since other reports allow initiating nawāfil during these times.
